candidate.title: discover and authorize bridge
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. disable ap/client isolation; bridge is powered and reachable.
candidate.steps:
1. open tv hue linkage settings and start lan discovery.
2. select the intended bridge and complete physical-button authorization/pairing.
3. inspect the active configuration and observe a physical lamp response.
candidate.expected: the intended supported bridge is discovered and bound. the linked configuration is usable and the physical light responds. record discovery duration; the sources do not define a release discovery deadline.

candidate.title: multi-bridge selection and switching
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. two supported bridges have distinguishable identifiers and eligible lights.
candidate.steps:
1. search for reachable bridges and bind the first selected bridge.
2. switch pairing to the second bridge.
3. inspect the active bridge and observe lights assigned to both bridges.
candidate.expected: only one bridge is active for simultaneous linkage. the selected bridge's lights follow the configuration; switching does not leave both bridges concurrently linked.

candidate.title: discover and add eligible linked lights
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. identify lamp capabilities and prepare a scene within 16 lights.
candidate.steps:
1. open linked-light device configuration and scan paired lights.
2. select supported lamps according to their color capabilities and inspect the scene.
3. trigger a configured color or temperature change and observe each selected lamp.
candidate.expected: supported color/extended color lamps and lightstrip can link dynamically. white ambiance provides temperature adjustment only; plain white is not a dynamic-color lamp. the scene contains no more than 16 linked lights.

candidate.title: movie mode physical light linkage
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. select movie mode and record response-speed settings and the observation endpoints.
candidate.steps:
1. play the controlled color-rich movie clip.
2. record the screen transition, tv backlight and hue physical response in a synchronized timebase.
3. measure elapsed response time and inspect color transition smoothness.
candidate.expected: movie mode target <= 200 ms; the sop p95 movie target is <= 200 ms. external hue end-to-end ceiling <= 1 s. lights follow the configured content with smooth transitions and no visible desynchronization. keep endpoint-specific measurements distinct; if mode-target endpoint applicability is unresolved for the release, mark the mode verdict pending clarification instead of certifying it.

candidate.title: game mode physical light linkage
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. select game mode and record response-speed settings and the observation endpoints.
candidate.steps:
1. play the rapid controlled color-change game scene.
2. record the screen transition, tv backlight and hue physical response in a synchronized timebase.
3. measure elapsed response time and inspect color transition smoothness.
candidate.expected: game mode target <= 100 ms; the sop p95 game target is <= 100 ms. external hue end-to-end ceiling <= 1 s. lights follow the configured content with smooth transitions and no visible desynchronization. keep endpoint-specific measurements distinct; if mode-target endpoint applicability is unresolved for the release, mark the mode verdict pending clarification instead of certifying it.

candidate.title: music rhythm linkage
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. select music mode and record rhythm algorithm and sensitivity.
candidate.steps:
1. play rhythm-intensive audio and vary tempo and volume.
2. observe physical lamp pulsing against the synchronized audio events.
3. measure elapsed music response time and inspect drift or stutter.
candidate.expected: music mode target <= 150 ms for the declared metric. lamps pulse according to the selected algorithm without stuttering or accumulated drift. a tempo change is not a universal promise of one fixed frequency relationship.

candidate.title: fixed-color always-on profile
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. verify the release supports the selected fixed-color/always-on profile and its hue applicability.
candidate.steps:
1. select a supported fixed-color profile and set a chosen color.
2. observe tv backlight and applicable linked lights over time.
3. record whether video changes affect the fixed effect.
candidate.expected: the supported fixed-color profile maintains the configured static effect without unintended flicker. external-lamp behavior is conditional on supported profile applicability; missing release confirmation blocks certification rather than implying support.

candidate.title: voice-controlled mode switching
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. bind a supported voice platform and the relevant account; verify command/mode applicability.
candidate.steps:
1. issue a supported voice command for movie mode, then game mode.
2. measure from command issuance to completed action.
3. observe actual tv mode and physical hue effect, not just platform status.
candidate.expected: voice command completes within 2 s and the requested supported mode is reflected in physical lighting. account/platform status alone does not prove execution.

candidate.title: paired-frame latency distribution
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. use controlled lighting, a color-step clip and a synchronized camera/timebase; record actual fps and endpoints.
candidate.steps:
1. record screen color changes and physical light responses together.
2. pair each response frame with its triggering screen frame.
3. calculate delay_ms = 1000 * (response_frame - trigger_frame) / fps, or subtract timestamps in the same timebase.
4. repeat across events and compute p95 using a stated percentile convention; retain raw paired observations.
candidate.expected: the elapsed latency is a response-minus-trigger duration, not an absolute timestamp. game target <= 100 ms; movie target <= 200 ms; hue ceiling <= 1 s. applicable game/movie p95 gates use the sop targets. quantization is derived from actual fps; unresolved endpoint scope is qualified. no unanchored percentage standard-deviation gate is used.
candidate.remarks: sources: spec-hue-amb-001 §6.1, §7.4; sop terminology and exit item2.

candidate.title: app and tv manual-control arbitration
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. hue app can issue manual changes; record which documented release control policy applies.
candidate.steps:
1. adjust lighting from tv and record the physical state and app observation.
2. during active linkage issue a manual color change from the phone app.
3. measure handover/hold duration and observe the final control state; report successful trials as counts.
candidate.expected: apply the documented profile: tv regains control within 3 s, or the product-defined manual color is retained for 10 s before resumption. if profile selection is unknown, the timing verdict is pending. record state convergence rather than claiming an undocumented bidirectional 1s guarantee or population reliability from a small trial count.
candidate.remarks: sources: spec-hue-amb-001 §7.6; sop §2.2. the source itself gives alternative3s/10s policies; neither is silently selected.

candidate.title: fast-motion transition smoothness
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. prepare fast color-change and gradient clips; select and record mode and lighting.
candidate.steps:
1. play fast-motion/color-switch clips followed by a gradient clip.
2. observe physical transitions and record abnormal frames, jumps, stutter and flicker.
3. when making a frequency-band claim, document instrument sampling bandwidth.
candidate.expected: transitions have no stepped abrupt changes or visible flicker. assess the specified high-frequency suppression only with adequate measurement bandwidth; a qualitative observation does not certify an unobserved frequency band.

candidate.title: concurrent multi-light response
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. prepare multiple eligible lights; this plan chooses eight as a stimulus, within the 16-light scene limit. record entertainment area setup.
candidate.steps:
1. select all test lights and play controlled/color-rich transitions.
2. record screen-to-response delay for every light and compute the maximum delay.
3. observe physical consistency, disconnects and any available diagnostic counters.
candidate.expected: all configured eligible lights respond; external hue delay <= 1 s for each lamp, with any stricter applicable mode metric evaluated separately. the scene does not exceed 16 lamps. cpu measurements are diagnostic without an approved limit; inaccessible bridge counters are not fabricated.

candidate.title: bridge network/power interruption
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. play video with working linkage and distinguish bridge ethernet from tv wi-fi.
candidate.steps:
1. interrupt bridge ethernet or power during linkage.
2. observe the hue physical state and independent tv backlight/playback.
3. time the app offline notification from the actual interruption.
candidate.expected: hue lamps maintain the last known state. tv ambilight continues normal operation without crash. the app offline prompt occurs within 5 s; this is not a tv-prompt requirement.

candidate.title: recovery after restored bridge network
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. execute a bridge network/power interruption first; record the retained configuration.
candidate.steps:
1. restore the bridge connection or power.
2. start recovery timing when connectivity is restored, without initiating rebinding.
3. observe automatic reconnection and resumed physical light sync.
candidate.expected: automatic reconnection/resumed sync is complete within 30 s of restored connectivity, without manual rebinding or abnormal flicker.

candidate.title: single-lamp power interruption
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. link more than one light and identify one lamp for power removal.
candidate.steps:
1. cut power to one selected lamp during linkage.
2. observe the remaining lights and tv, and time the app notification.
3. restore the lamp power and record its reintegration behavior without assuming a restart deadline.
candidate.expected: remaining lights continue sync and the tv has no lag/crash. the app light offline notification occurs within 10 s. individual-lamp restart timing is characterized; the source does not supply a restart sla.

candidate.title: concurrent game/movie mode triggers
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. movie linkage is active; game trigger is supported.
candidate.steps:
1. issue the game trigger during movie playback.
2. time and observe the selected active mode and physical transition.
3. inspect for freezing or visible flicker.
candidate.expected: game overrides the lower-priority competing mode under the documented ordering (game > football > movie > music > lounge light > custom.). mode transition <= 1 s without crash or visible flicker.

candidate.title: weak/degraded network characterization
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. apply impairment to the tv-bridge path using a network simulation tool; record the healthy baseline.
candidate.steps:
1. inject a documented test-choice latency/loss profile and observe timing, continuity and notifications.
2. increase impairment and record actual link loss or continued operation.
3. restore the baseline and, if a disconnect occurred, measure reconnect from restored connectivity.
candidate.expected: record degraded-network observations without an undocumented sla or mandatory packet-loss warning. if an actual disconnect occurs, lights hold their last state while tv remains operational. after restored connectivity automatic recovery <= 30 s. a release-specific degraded-network acceptance profile remains conditional on approval.

candidate.title: bridge firmware upgrade recovery
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. record the existing configuration and have an authorized bridge upgrade available.
candidate.steps:
1. initiate the bridge firmware upgrade in app and observe linkage unavailability.
2. observe completion and restoration of the recorded configuration.
3. for a controlled timeout variant, observe the manual-check prompt when recovery does not occur.
candidate.expected: linkage is temporarily unavailable during upgrade. after completion the configuration restores automatically without re-pairing. if upgrade exceeds 120 s without recovery, prompt manual checking. arbitrary flashing/reset is not certified as expected.

candidate.title: daylight ambient-light adaptation
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. use an als-capable unit, enable adaptive brightness for this case and prepare measured daylight above 300 lux within the sensor range. record manual cap/override and fixed content.
candidate.steps:
1. measure a controlled reference brightness.
2. increase ambient illuminance and record physical brightness/contrast with unchanged mode/content.
3. observe transitions and restore the baseline adaptive setting after the case.
candidate.expected: at the documented daylight condition, tv ambilight increases adaptive brightness/contrast subject to the manual limit. external hue inheritance is conditional on release capability; do not certify it from the tv-only statement. no unsupported fixed percentage rise is required.

candidate.title: night/pitch-black adaptive brightness
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. enable als adaptation, record the reference brightness and manual cap, and control night lighting below 50 lux separately from pitch black below 5 lux.
candidate.steps:
1. with fixed content/mode measure reference brightness, then the night output.
2. calculate reduction_pct = 100*(reference - night)/reference.
3. measure a separate pitch-black condition and observe the minimum-brightness effect.
candidate.expected: in the night region brightness reduces by 50%-70% relative to the defined baseline. in pitch black (< 5 lux), minimum brightness retains a faint halo. this is not an absolute output below30%. external hue applicability and the reference condition are explicitly qualified.

candidate.title: 72-hour linkage stability
candidate.preconditions: record tv, bridge, lamp and app versions. use a supported tv/build, ethernet bridge on the same subnet/vlan as the tv, and eligible paired lights. prepare automated playback/mode changes, monitoring and a post-warm-up baseline for the same measured process.
candidate.steps:
1. run the planned sequence for 72 hours with a documented switching/sampling schedule.
2. log crashes, freezes, continuity and available cpu/memory diagnostics.
3. calculate memory growth_pct =100*(final_memory - baseline_memory)/baseline_memory using the same process/metric.
candidate.expected: no crash or freeze during 72 h. memory growth < 5% after the run. cpu limits and a population linkage-success guarantee are not invented; retain observed counts and resource trends.

Philips Hue & Ambilight Function Specification
1. Document Information
Document Number: SPEC-HUE-AMB-001
Version: V1.0
Date: 2026-09-18
Scope: Philips TV Ambilight and Philips Hue Smart Lighting Integration
Classification: Internal / Confidential
Version History
2. Introduction
2.1 Purpose
This document defines the complete functional specification for the Ambilight feature, encompassing hardware layout, color and brightness control, response synchronization mechanisms, and intelligent linkage capabilities with Philips Hue.
2.2 Scope
This specification covers all Philips TV models supporting Ambilight and their integration with Philips Hue smart lighting products.
2.3 Target Audience
Functional Test Engineers
Product Managers
Hardware Engineers
Firmware Developers
2.4 References
IEC 62471: Photobiological Safety of Lamps and Lamp Systems
ENERGY STAR Program Requirements for Televisions
3. Functional Overview
3.1 System Architecture
The system comprises the TV-side Ambilight processor, LED strip arrays, Philips Hue Bridge, and Hue lamps. Data flows from the TV video processor to the Ambilight controller, which outputs to the TV LEDs and simultaneously sends sync commands via Wi-Fi to the Hue Bridge, which translates them to Zigbee signals for Hue lamps.
3.2 Key Features Summary
Dynamic Color Mapping
Multi-mode Switching
Hue Whole-home Linkage
Audio Synchronization
Ambient Light Adaptation
Voice Control
Shutdown Fade Out
Custom Scenes
3.3 Not in Scope
Hue lamp firmware upgrades
Compatibility with non-Philips third-party lamps
HDR tone mapping algorithms
4. Hardware Layout Specification
4.1 LED Strip Configuration
Entry Level: Left and right sides only; 24-32 LEDs.
Mid Range: Left, right, and top sides; 40-57 LEDs.
High End: Full four-sided surround; 60+ LEDs.
OLED Flagship: 360-degree surround with pixel-level light sync.
4.2 Installation Requirements
Distance from Wall: Recommended 10-25cm (Optimal: 10-15cm).
Wall Color: White, neutral, or light-colored flat surfaces.
Ambient Light: Avoid direct strong light on the LED strip area.
Installation Angle: LED strip to wall angle should be ≤30°.
4.3 LED Technical Parameters
Color Gamut: Full sRGB coverage.
Brightness Range: 1%-100% adjustable.
Color Temperature (Warm White Mode): 2200K-4500K.
Response Time: < 10ms (Hardware level).
Power Consumption: < 15W in Ambilight mode.
5. Color & Brightness Control Specification
5.1 Dynamic Color Extraction
Real-time analysis of edge colors from input video signals (HDMI/Internal).
Processing Frame Rate: ≥ 30fps input corresponds to ≥ 30fps light effect update.
Color Mapping Precision: 8-bit per channel (256 levels/channel).
Color Transition Algorithm: Linear interpolation + gradient compensation.
5.2 Brightness Control
User Adjustable Levels: Low / Medium / High / Maximum (4 levels).
Auto Brightness: Adaptive based on ambient light sensor (0-1000 lux range).
Max Brightness Limit: User-lockable upper limit to prevent glare at night.
Brightness Adjustment Response Time: < 500ms.
5.3 Color Modes
Natural: Faithful reproduction of edge colors with smooth transitions; for daily viewing.
Vivid: Enhanced saturation and brightness; for variety shows/concerts.
Football: Enhanced green pitch tones; dynamic tracking of player movement.
Game: Lowest latency for high-speed画面 changes.
Music: Lights pulse to audio rhythm; supports multiple rhythm algorithms.
Lounge Light: 6500K soft static white light in standby/specific modes to reduce eye strain.
Warm White: Fixed warm white tone with adjustable color temperature.
Custom: User-defined fixed color via color palette.
5.4 Saturation Control
Adjustable Levels: 0-100%.
Default Value: 50%.
Adjustment Step: 10%.
5.5 Wall Color Compensation
Supported Wall Colors: White / Cream / Light Gray / Dark Gray / Custom.
TV automatically corrects Ambilight output to compensate for wall reflection.
Calibration Precision: CIE ΔE < 5.
5.6 Separation Control
Sets the color difference level between left and right lights.
Off: Uniform color presentation.
On: Enhanced stereoscopic effect.
Adjustable Levels: 0-10.
5.7 TV Off Fade Out
Option 1: Immediate Switch Off.
Option 2: Fade Out to Off. Adjustable fade time: 3s / 5s / 10s / 30s.
6. Response & Sync Mechanism Specification
6.1 End-to-End Latency Requirements
Game Mode: ≤ 100ms (Must Have)
Movie Mode: ≤ 200ms (Should Have)
Music Mode: ≤ 150ms (Should Have)
Natural Mode: ≤ 200ms (Should Have)
Vivid Mode: ≤ 150ms (Should Have)
Football Mode: ≤ 200ms (Should Have)
6.2 Responsiveness Adjustment
User-adjustable Ambilight response speed to screen changes (Slider: Slow / Normal / Fast).
Default: Normal.
Fast: Lowest latency but possible slight color jumps.
Slow: Smoothest transition but slightly higher latency.
6.3 Transition Smoothness
Color Transition: No stepped abrupt changes, no visible flicker.
High-frequency Flicker Suppression: > 50Hz flicker must be eliminated.
Gradient Color Video Test: Smooth transition to naked eye, no abrupt changes in light curve.
6.4 Motion Compensation (MEMC for Ambilight)
Predicts画面 change trends via motion estimation and compensation algorithms.
Adjusts light transitions in advance to avoid disconnection between画面 and lights.
Applicable Scenarios: Game / Football / Vivid modes.
7. Philips Hue Linkage Specification
7.1 Connection Protocol
Communication: Wi-Fi (TV side) + Zigbee (Bridge side).
Bridge Compatibility: Philips Hue Bridge 2.0 and above.
Max Supported Hue Lamps: 16 per linkage scene.
Discovery Protocol: mDNS/Bonjour LAN discovery.
Pairing Flow: TV search → User selects Bridge → User confirms pairing → Auto-discover lamps.
7.2 Compatible Hue Lamp Types
Color Light: Supported.
Extended Color Light: Supported.
White Ambiance: Supported (Color temperature adjustment only).
White: Not supported for dynamic color linkage.
LightStrip: Supported.
Not Supported: Non-Philips brand lamps, 1st Gen Hue Bridge (v1).
7.3 Linkage Modes
Movie Mode Sync: Hue lamps sync with Ambilight colors during movies.
Game Mode Sync: Hue lamps sync with game light effects.
Music Mode Sync: Hue lamps pulse to audio rhythm.
Party Mode: Festive gathering mode; Hue lamps sync with Ambilight for colorful gradient switching.
Custom Scene: User-defined scene rules (e.g., “Dim ceiling lights + Activate surround light effects when watching movies”).
7.4 Linkage Latency
TV → Bridge Command Delay: ≤ 500ms.
Bridge → Hue Lamp Response Delay: ≤ 300ms.
End-to-End (TV画面 change → Hue lamp color change): ≤ 1s (Must Have).
7.5 Linkage Configuration
Enable/Disable: Settings > Display & Sound > Ambilight > AMBILIGHT EXTENSION > Hue > Enable/Disable.
Configuration: Select and set each Hue lamp to follow Ambilight colors.
View Configuration: View current setup of network, Bridge, and bulbs.
Reset Configuration: Reset current setup.
7.6 Hue Linkage Behavior Rules
Network Disconnection: Hue lamps maintain last known state; no flickering or error reporting.
Network Recovery: Auto-reconnect and resume sync within 30s.
Manual Control Conflict: When manually adjusting lights via phone App, TV regains control within 3s (or maintains manual color for 10s before resuming, per product definition).
Multi-Bridge Scenario: Only 1 Bridge supported for simultaneous linkage.
8. Audio Sync Specification
8.1 Audio Follow Mode
Lights pulse to audio spectrum rhythm.
Supported Modes: Music / Game.
Rhythm Algorithm Types: Pulse / Gradient / Color Fluctuation (Switchable).
Sensitivity Adjustment: Low / Medium / High.
8.2 Philips Wireless Home Speakers Linkage
TV and Philips Wireless Home Speakers connect via Wi-Fi.
Linkage Content: Ambilight light effects change with speaker volume/frequency.
Configuration Path: Settings > Display & Sound > Ambilight > AMBILIGHT EXTENSION > Philips Wireless Home Speakers.
9. Ambient Light Adaptive Specification
9.1 Sensor Requirements
Sensor Type: Ambient Light Sensor (ALS).
Detection Range: 0 - 1000 lux.
Sampling Frequency: ≥ 1Hz.
Calibration: Factory calibration + User manual calibration.
9.2 Adaptive Behavior
Daytime (> 300 lux): Enhanced LED brightness and contrast.
Evening (50-300 lux): Medium brightness.
Night (< 50 lux): Auto-reduce brightness by 50%-70% to prevent glare.
Pitch Black (< 5 lux): Minimum brightness mode; only faint halo retained.
9.3 Manual Override
User can disable auto-brightness anytime and set fixed brightness levels.
When auto-brightness is off, sensor enters low-power standby mode.
10. Voice Control Specification
10.1 Supported Platforms
Google Assistant
Amazon Alexa
Apple HomeKit (Siri)
Samsung SmartThings
10.2 Voice Commands
“Hey Siri/Google, Turn on Ambilight Movie Mode”
“Hey Google, set Hue lights to Ambilight sync”
“Alexa, turn off Hue Sync”
“Hey Siri, set Ambilight to Game mode”
10.3 Voice Control Response Time
Command to Execution Completion: ≤ 2s (Must Have).
Command Recognition Accuracy: ≥ 95% (Standard environment).
11. Power Management Specification
11.1 Power Consumption
Ambilight On (Medium Brightness): ≤ 12W.
Ambilight On (Max Brightness): ≤ 15W.
Ambilight Off: ≤ 0.5W (Standby).
Hue Linkage Standby (TV off, Bridge online): ≤ 1.0W.
11.2 Power Saving Modes
Auto Sleep: Ambilight auto-off after 5 minutes of no画面 input.
Timed Off: User-settable timer (30min / 60min / 90min).
Energy Saving Mode: Brightness auto-limited to below 50%.
12. Error Handling & Recovery Specification
12.1 Network Failure
TV & Bridge Disconnection: Hue lamps maintain last state; TV Ambilight continues normal operation.
Recovery Time: Auto-reconnect within 30s after network recovery.
User Prompt: App displays offline prompt within 5s.
12.2 Device Offline
Single Hue Lamp Power Off: Remaining lamps continue sync; TV side no lag.
Prompt: App displays “Light Offline” notification within 10s.
12.3 Bridge Firmware Upgrade
During Upgrade: Linkage function temporarily unavailable.
Post-Upgrade: Auto-restore configuration; no re-pairing needed.
Timeout Handling: If upgrade exceeds 120s without recovery, prompt user for manual check.
12.4 Concurrent Trigger Conflict
Priority (High to Low): Game > Football > Movie > Music > Lounge Light > Custom.
Conflict Handling: Higher priority mode overrides lower priority; transition time ≤ 1s.
13. Performance Requirements Summary
14. Terminology
Ambilight: Philips’ proprietary ambient lighting technology that projects colors from the TV screen onto the surrounding wall.
Hue Bridge: The central hub that connects Philips Hue lamps to the TV and network.
Zigbee: Wireless communication protocol used between Hue Bridge and Hue lamps.
MEMC: Motion Estimation and Motion Compensation; algorithm to predict画面 changes for smoother light transitions.
CIE ΔE: Metric for color difference; lower values indicate higher color accuracy.
Lux: Unit of illuminance used to measure ambient light levels.
PWM: Pulse Width Modulation; technique for controlling LED brightness.
mDNS: Multicast DNS; protocol for local network device discovery.
Hue Entertainment Area: Group of Hue lamps configured for synchronized light effects.
Lounge Light: Static ambient light mode for relaxed viewing.
Warm White: Fixed warm color temperature light mode.
Color Light: Hue lamp capable of displaying multiple colors.
Extended Color Light: Hue lamp with wider color gamut and color temperature control.
End-to-End Latency: Total time from画面 change to light effect update.
Fade Out: Gradual dimming of lights when TV is turned off.
Wall Color Compensation: Algorithm to adjust light output based on wall color.
Separation: Control of color difference between left and right Ambilight zones.
ALS: Ambient Light Sensor; detects room lighting for auto-brightness.
Chromasync: Proprietary synchronization protocol between TV and Hue lamps.
15. Revision History
Version | Date | Author | Reviewer | Approver | Description
V1.0 | 2026-09-18 | R&D | PM | QA Lead | Initial Release
Metric | Requirement | Priority
Game Mode End-to-End Latency | ≤ 100ms | Must Have
Movie Mode End-to-End Latency | ≤ 200ms | Should Have
Music Mode End-to-End Latency | ≤ 150ms | Should Have
Hue Linkage End-to-End Latency | ≤ 1s | Must Have
Color Transition Smoothness | No stepped abrupt changes | Must Have
Network Recovery Time | ≤ 30s | Must Have
Voice Control Response Time | ≤ 2s | Must Have
Flicker Suppression | > 50Hz no visible flicker | Must Have
72h Stability | No crash / No memory leak | Should Have

Philips Hue & Ambilight Linkage Test SOP
1. Environment Setup
1.1 Network Environment
Set up a dedicated 5GHz Wi-Fi test network to ensure no interference from other IoT devices. Enterprise-grade routers are recommended, with power-saving mode disabled. - Acceptance Criteria: Signal strength > -65dBm, packet loss rate 0% - TV and Bridge connected to the same subnet (same VLAN) - Disable AP Isolation / Client Isolation on the router - Avoid using public Wi-Fi or guest networks - If conditions permit, test separately on both 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands
1.2 Philips Hue Bridge Configuration
Connect the Philips Hue Bridge to the test network, ensuring the firmware is the latest stable version and bound to the test account. - Record and archive Bridge firmware version (different firmware versions may affect linkage behavior) - App displays “Connected” with no offline devices - Bridge connected to the router via Ethernet cable (Wi-Fi bridging mode is prohibited) - Confirm Bridge has been added to the Philips Hue App and can be controlled normally - If using a Hue Entertainment Area, confirm the entertainment area scope is configured correctly
1.3 Light Deployment
Deploy 2-4 Hue lights within 1-2 meters behind the TV (covering left/right/rear areas). - Lights are unobstructed with normal Zigbee signal (signal strength > -70dBm) - Lights are evenly distributed around the TV, avoiding concentration on one side - Record model, firmware version, and installation position for each light - Prepare 4-6 lights if testing multi-light concurrent scenarios - Ensure stable power supply for lights; use original power adapters
1.4 TV Configuration
Go to Settings > Ambilight > Philips Hue, enable linkage, and select “Standard/Game/Movie” mode. - Status displays “Hue Sync Active” - Record TV system version and Ambilight firmware version - Disable TV “Power Saving Mode” and “Auto Brightness Adjustment” (to avoid interfering with test results) - Confirm Ambilight color calibration has been performed (if supported) - If testing voice control, confirm third-party voice assistants (Siri/Google Home/Alexa) are bound
1.5 Test Material Preparation
Prepare standard test videos and images covering all Ambilight mode scenarios. - Color block jump video (rapid switching of red/green/blue/white/black for latency testing) - Gradient color video (slow color transition for smoothness testing) - Fast motion scenes (racing, explosion effects for dynamic tracking testing) - Starry sky/night scene video (low brightness scenes for dark field performance testing) - Solid color images (full white/full black/full red/full green/full blue for baseline calibration) - Sports match footage (green lawn + dynamic crowd for color reproduction testing) - Music rhythm video (lights changing with rhythm for music mode testing)
1.6 Environmental Requirements
The test environment must meet the following physical conditions to ensure repeatability and accuracy of test results. - Indoor Lighting: Prepare adjustable blackout curtains supporting three environments: full dark / semi-light / full light - Room Temperature: 20-25°C, avoid direct air conditioning blowing on TV or lights - Wall Color: White or light gray walls (dark walls absorb light and affect observation) - TV Installation: Wall-mounted or placed on a flat table, with 5-10cm distance between the back and the wall - Record environmental parameters for each test (temperature, lighting, TV mode)
2. Test Scope
2.1 Functional Scope
This SOP covers the following linkage scenarios between Philips TV Ambilight function and Philips Hue smart lighting: - Ambilight Basic Mode Linkage: Standard, Vivid, Movie, Game, Music, Always On - Philips Hue Device Discovery & Binding: TV-side automatic Bridge search, supporting multi-Bridge scenarios - Scene Mode Switching: Hue light color temperature, saturation, and brightness linkage under different Ambilight modes - Voice Control Linkage: Controlling light sync on/off via Siri / Google Home / Alexa - Fault Recovery: Automatic recovery mechanism after network disconnection, power outage, or Bridge offline - Multi-device Concurrency: Color consistency and response latency when multiple Hue lights sync simultaneously
2.2 Items Out of Scope
Electrical characteristic testing at the Hue bulb hardware level (belongs to hardware testing)
Zigbee protocol stack underlying communication debugging (belongs to protocol layer testing)
MQTT/HTTP network packet capture analysis (belongs to network debugging)
Pixel-level color accuracy testing of the TV Ambilight light strip itself (belongs to picture quality testing)
UI/UX functional testing of the Philips Hue App itself

The following defect severity standards are used to unify the test team’s judgment on defect severity and ensure standardized defect management.
4.1 Defect Priority
Defect priority guides the repair sequence and does not necessarily correspond one-to-one with severity level: - P0/P1: Fix Now - P2: Fix Next (schedule for current iteration) - P3/P4: Backlog (schedule when available)
5. Troubleshooting
The following lists common issues and troubleshooting directions that may be encountered during testing for test engineers’ reference.
6. Tips for Test Engineers
Tip 1 — Do Not Rely Solely on App Status: If the App shows “Syncing” but lights are not on, it is usually due to Zigbee congestion or bulb firmware issues; physical performance must be observed. It is recommended to visually confirm the actual lighting status of the lights during each test rather than relying solely on the App status bar.
Tip 2 — Ambient Light Interference: When testing latency, be sure to close curtains/turn off lights to avoid ambient light reflecting off walls and interfering with camera recognition. It is recommended to cover the test area with blackout cloth to ensure consistent lighting conditions.
Tip 3 — Zigbee Congestion: If latency spikes when testing more than 4 lights, first check if Hue Entertainment Area is enabled. This mode requires extremely high bandwidth; ensure Bridge performance is sufficient. You can try halving the number of lights in the entertainment area for comparison testing.
Tip 4 — Firmware Version Recording: Record TV system version, Ambilight firmware version, Bridge firmware version, and Hue App version before each test. Different version combinations may lead to different linkage behaviors; version information is a key clue for defect troubleshooting.
Tip 5 — Test Data Archiving: It is recommended to archive latency data, environmental parameters, and test results for each test to a shared directory using the naming convention “Date_Test Scenario_Environmental Parameters” to facilitate subsequent trend analysis and regression test comparison.
Tip 6 — Multi-scenario Cross-validation: It is recommended to test linkage functions under different TV signal sources (HDMI 1/2/3, Built-in Apps, Screen Casting). The image processing pipeline of different signal sources may affect Ambilight analysis latency.
Tip 7 — Regression Testing Recommendation: After each TV system update or Bridge firmware upgrade, it is recommended to execute the complete regression test process, focusing on the two core scenarios of network recovery and mode switching.

3. System Overview
3.1 Architecture
Philips Hue is a personal wireless lighting system by Signify that combines LED illumination with wireless connectivity. The system architecture consists of:
Hue Bridge / Bridge Pro — Central hub connecting to the home router via Ethernet, managing all Zigbee devices via the Zigbee mesh network
Smart Lights — LED bulbs, lightstrips, and fixtures that communicate via Zigbee (and Bluetooth on supported models)
Accessories — Motion sensors, dimmer switches, smart plugs that extend functionality
Cloud & Apps — Philips Hue Bridge API (REST), Philips Hue App (iOS/Android), third-party integrations (Apple HomeKit, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings)
3.2 System Topology

Automation & Scheduling — Time-based, sunrise/sunset, geofencing (away/home detection)
Hue Sync — Lights sync to TV screen content, games, and music via HDMI sync box or desktop app
Hue Secure — Integration with security cameras and motion sensors for alarm triggering
Voice Control — Alexa, Google Home, Apple HomeKit, Samsung SmartThings
MotionAware — Use lights as motion sensors via Zigbee signal strength measurement (Bridge Pro only)
Away-from-Home Control — Control lights remotely via internet connection
Third-party Ecosystem — IFTTT integration for weather, email, sports, and more

8. Connection & Setup Guide
8.1 Connection Methods Overview
Philips Hue supports three primary connection methods. Choose based on your needs:
8.2 Method 1: Hue Bridge Connection (Recommended)
Step 1: Hardware Setup
Plug the Hue Bridge power adapter into a nearby electrical outlet.
Connect the Hue Bridge to your Wi-Fi router using the included Ethernet cable (RJ-45).
Wait for the Bridge indicator lights to illuminate (first 3 LEDs lighting up indicates successful connection).
Step 2: Network Configuration
Ensure your router is powered on and providing internet access.
The Bridge will automatically obtain an IP address via DHCP.
Verify connectivity: the Bridge’s front LED should glow solid white.
Step 3: App Setup
Download the “Philips Hue” app from the App Store (iOS) or Google Play Store (Android).
Open the app and create or log in to your Philips Hue account.
Navigate to Settings > Devices > Tap the blue “+” icon.
Select “Add Bridge” and follow the on-screen prompts.
Press the physical button on the Bridge for 3 seconds to authorize the app.
Step 4: Adding Lights
In the app, go to Settings > Devices > Tap “+” > “Add Light.”
If your light has a QR code, scan it.
If no QR code, select “No QR Code” and the app will search for nearby lights.
Alternatively, enter the serial number manually.
Name your light and assign it to a room.
Step 5: Verification
Open the app and toggle lights on/off to verify connectivity.
Check that all lights respond within 1 second.
8.3 Method 2: Bluetooth Direct Connection (No Bridge Required)
Prerequisites
Ensure Bluetooth is enabled on your phone.
Lights must be within Bluetooth range (~10 m, single room).
At least one Hue light must be powered on.
Steps
Open the Philips Hue app.
Go to Settings > Devices > Tap “+” to add device.
Scan the QR code on the light or lightstrip packaging.
Follow the pairing prompts.
The app will discover and add the light directly via BLE.
Limitations
Maximum 10 lights per Bluetooth connection.
Control limited to single room only.
No away-from-home control.
No automation/scheduling (unless Bridge is added later).
No Hue Sync, Hue Secure, or voice control.
8.4 Method 3: Matter Protocol Connection
Prerequisites
A Matter-compatible controller (Apple HomePod Mini, Google Nest Hub, etc.).
Matter-enabled Hue lights (most 2023+ models).
Thread border router (if using Matter over Thread).
Steps
Open your smart home app (Apple Home, Google Home, etc.).
Select “Add Device” or “Add Accessory.”
Scan the Matter QR code on the light’s installation guide.
Enter the 11-digit pairing code if QR is unavailable.
Ensure the light is in pairing mode (flashing/blinking).
Complete the on-screen setup.
8.5 Adding Hue Bridge Pro
The Bridge Pro setup is similar to the standard Bridge with additional steps:
Hardware: Connect Bridge Pro to power and Ethernet (or Wi-Fi).
App: The app will detect the Bridge Pro automatically.
Firmware: The Bridge Pro will prompt for a firmware update on first setup. Allow this to complete (may take 2-5 minutes).
Device Count: After setup, verify device count in Settings > About Bridge Pro.
